medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students interested in taking a leave of absence may speak with the Director of Student Support Services.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: We offer over 50 student organizations, including a student-run clinic as well as intramural teams, 3 residential fraternities, student council, an orchestra and student-run publications.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Twin Cities Campus is located on the second largest university campus in the United States. Most major hospitals in the Minneapolis/St. Paul metro are affiliated with the Medical School.

Duluth Campus is located in northeastern Minnesota dedicated to​ serving the needs of rural and Native American/American Indian communities.

St. Cloud Campus is along the Sauk River, partnering with CentraCare to educate future physicians who aspire to be great clinicians and leaders across ​Greater Minnesota, both rural and immigrant communities.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Medical student fraternities [TC] and private housing are available in the campus neighborhoods; both campuses maintain a list of resources for affordable off-campus housing.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Minnesota is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. The University of Minnesota campus offers the following resources http://diversity.umn.edu/. For additional information regarding active student groups/support please email medadmis@umn.edu.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Office of Learner Development's goal is to assist students in identifying ways of adapting learning approaches to meet the unique challenges of medical education, and in developing skills for lifelong learning, success and satisfaction in medicine.
All students are matched with an Academic Faculty Advisor. Together students and advisors will build longitudinal relationships and peer communities that foster reflection and growth. Advisors facilitate student's personal and professional development. 
The Medical Student-led Wellbeing Committee strives to support and promote the wellbeing of medical students by providing resources, building relationships, and cultivating an environment to foster the health of the whole person.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Across all three campuses, students will have the opportunity to participate in hybrid learning, this includes but is not limited to in-person learning, small group learning and asynchronous learning. We believe in early patient exposure and have created opportunities in the first two years for clinical experiences. We value student input and encourage students to provide feedback through years 1-4.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Strongly encourage/recommend having transportation means to travel to clinical sites.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: We ask students to dress appropriately, including wearing a clean white coat and/or appropriate identification during all anticipated patient contact.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Academic support services are available to all medical students through the Office of Learner Development, which offers help to increase study effectiveness and achieve educational milestones.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Patient interactions begin Spring of the first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Our curriculum incorporates large lecture formats, including active learning strategies, small group discussions built into most courses, labs, as well as small group case study based courses.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin in the third year.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Some lectures do require mandatory attendance, and are also determined by the course directors. All lectures are recorded, so students have the ability to access the material outside of lecture time.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Our curriculum offers integrated instruction in scientific foundations of medicine and clinical sciences. An emphasis on critical thinking and self-directed learning is built into courses. The curriculum offers early clinical exposure with students seeing patients in the clinical learning environment in January of their first year. The second phase of the curriculum, Clinical Immersion, allows students to complete comprehensive clinical training and work in a variety of specialty environments to explore possible specialty interests. The third phase of the curriculum is design to individualize each student's preparation for the transition to residency, with specially designed experiences to either identify a specialty of interest or to prepare for residency in a chosen specialty. Each student has an advisor to ensure achievement of required competencies. The Twin Cities campus offers a Medical Scientist Training Program and other combined degrees, while the St. Cloud campus has a focus in rural primary care and the Duluth campus has a mission focused on preparing students for practice in rural Minnesota and Native American communities.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The University of Minnesota has a strong commitment to primary care, starting with the Duluth campus, which is committed to family medicine. Both the Duluth and Twin Cities students can participate in the Rural Physician Associate Program and the Metropolitan Physician Associate Program, which focus on primary care. We also have the largest family medicine residency program in the country. The Duluth Campus is a national leader for graduating family medicine physicians.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Our research ranges from investigating the innermost workings of cells to analyzing health data at a population level. Our faculty searches for answers to who is susceptible to disease, and why. The results lead to new ways for preventive care, to treatments for some of the most complex and devastating diseases. We are leaders in diabetes, neuroscience, cardiovascular disease, cancer, and infectious disease research. Currently, researchers at the University's Center for Magnetic Resonance Research are mapping the connections of the human brain.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Though research is not required, it is encouraged and well supported.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The Medical School has over 26 teaching hospitals and 31 clinical training sites with which it is affiliated.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Students in years 1 and 2 will receive grades of Pass or No Pass. Students in years 3 and 4 will receive grades of Honors, Excellent, Satisfactory, or No Pass.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Founded in 1888, the University of Minnesota Medical School has three campuses.  MD programs are located on the Twin Cities and our two regional campuses in Duluth and St. Cloud. The Twin Cities also hosts an MD/PhD program.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The Mission of the University of Minnesota Medical School is to be a leader in enhancing the health of people through the education of skilled, compassionate and socially responsible physicians. With three campuses serving diverse populations in rural and urban Minnesota, the Medical School is dedicated to preeminent primary care medicine, exemplary specialty care and innovative research.

In addition to the overall Mission, the Duluth campus has a unique focus on rural and American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) health and family medicine with a mission to be a national leader in improving healthcare access and outcomes in rural Minnesota and AI/AN communities. In partnership with CentraCare, the regional campus in St. Cloud offers a wide range of patient experiences throughout students’ education in Greater Minnesota and prepares them to become exceptional clinicians and leaders for rural and immigrant populations.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege: The University of Minnesota, College of Liberal Arts.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
The Bachelor of Arts/Medical Doctor (BA/MD) Scholars Program provides a unique opportunity for exceptional Minnesota residents to become physicians committed to meeting the healthcare needs of all Minnesotans. Students invited to apply are high achieving high school seniors who demonstrate an early interest in medicine. The program includes students from rural communities and medically-underserved communities, first-generation college students, and those from economically disadvantaged backgrounds. Selection for this program is highly competitive, with a small cohort entering the program as incoming freshmen each fall. Selection decisions will not consider race, gender, or other protected characteristics consistent with legal requirements.

This invitation-only, specialized support program is a partnership between the College of Liberal Arts (CLA) and the Medical School at the University of Minnesota.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Where you pursue your MD/PhD education is no small decision. We would like to help you learn how the University of Minnesota Medical Scientist Training Program can help you reach your educational and career goals. 

https://med.umn.edu/education-training/medical-scientist-training-program-mdphd/mstp-admissions

The Military Medic to Medical School program is a one year program that serves as a bridge from military to civilian medical experiences in preparation for matriculation into medical school at UMMS through early assurance.  In a cohort model, we provide individualized support and advising in multiple tracks that are designed to serve as a pathway to medical school for current and former military medics. Strongest candidates for the program will have at least 3 years of operational military medical experience, preferably with deployment, have completed the majority of prerequisites for medical school admission, and demonstrate their academic ability to have success in medical school. Included in the program are two semesters of a seminar course at the University of Minnesota, Kaplan MCAT prep for those who have not yet taken the MCAT, and opportunities for research, clinical exposure, and mentoring by medical school faculty.  For more info, email Chris VanBrenk at vanbr049@umn.edu.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Applicants can complete the required prerequisite coursework at any accredited U.S. or Canadian institutions.  All admission requirements including required courses and undergraduate degree must be completed prior to matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We recommend no more than 10 years.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Legal residents of Minnesota are given preference but qualified out-of-state applicants are encouraged to apply. The Medical School reviews each application holistically, focusing on 9 core competencies (academic readiness, intellectual inquiry, service orientation, growth mindset, critical thinking, cultural humility, empathy and compassion, ethical responsibility as well as teamwork and leadership). Applicants are evaluated through recommendation letters, experiences, undergraduate education and academics, responses to the supplemental application, as well as interviews. In addition, the Duluth campus seeks individuals with interest and experiences that support a commitment to rural Minnesota and American Indian/Alaska Native communities. Applicants interested in the CentraCare St. Cloud campus should aspire to be outstanding clinicians and leaders across Greater Minnesota. Students accepted to the Twin Cities campus enter a class of 165 MD candidates, Duluth 65, and St. Cloud 24.
